cases.name: progressive_hits
cases.description: Identical over-limit hits from a hardened shell. The plate loses integrity every hit, its softening strength lowers the plateau so later hits charge slightly more, and it fails after a finite count while the harder shell stays elastic.

cases.name: quantity_and_thickness
cases.description: Capacity scales with represented volume, so twice the plate takes about twice the hits. Doubling the represented thickness doubles the load-bearing area and halves the stress, so a hit that dents the thin plate stays recoverable on the thick one.

rows.label: plate volume 20 wu^3: fails after 9 hits at 300 wu/s
plate volume 40 wu^3: fails after 18 hits at 300 wu/s
plate thickness 1 wu: one hit at 1.658 wu/s, 1.2x the thin plate's safe-limit speed
plate thickness 2 wu: one hit at 1.658 wu/s, 1.2x the thin plate's safe-limit speed

cases.name: wood_vs_armor
cases.description: A falling branch against plate. Wood is the weaker material, so it carries the whole plateau and snaps, while the plate's irreversible work is exactly zero at any speed. The excess is energy the broken wood carries away.

rows.label: branch vs tank at 15 wu/s
branch vs tank at 40 wu/s
branch vs tank at 120 wu/s

cases.name: tissue_vs_wood
cases.description: The same stone at the same speed against soft tissue and against wood. Both are weaker than rock and yield, but tissue's small strength and capacity lose a far larger integrity fraction.

rows.label: stone vs spaceling at 10 wu/s
stone vs branch at 10 wu/s

cases.name: equal_strength_tie
cases.description: Two hulls of the same material: both reach the safe limit together and share the plateau work equally.

rows.label: ship vs ship at 20 wu/s

cases.name: severe_armor_failure
cases.description: A hardened shell with more energy than the plate can absorb. The plate's capacity is exhausted in one hit, the remainder is reported as excess that stays with the motion, the ledger still closes and nothing is infinite.

rows.label: shell vs tank at 600 wu/s
shell vs tank at 1200 wu/s

cases.name: glancing
cases.description: Only the normal component of the approach loads the contact. The same speed at a shallower incidence does strictly less work. Tangential loading is outside this model.

cases.name: angular
cases.description: An off-center hit spends part of the approach on spinning the boulder. The lever arm lowers the contact-effective mass, the available energy and the damage; a central hit is the upper bound.

cases.name: resting_support
cases.description: A safe resting load charges nothing however long it rests. An overload yields and charges plateau work each tick until the plank fails in bounded time, sooner for a larger overload; a host-measured plastic displacement replaces the fallback progression.

rows.label: tank resting on a wood plank: force 2000 over 2 wu^2 for 1000 ticks
press of force 6300, 1.05x the safe stress, fallback progression: fails after 3 ticks (0.050 s)
press of force 9000, 1.5x the safe stress, fallback progression: fails after 1 tick (0.017 s)
the 1.5x press with a measured 0.02 wu plastic displacement in one tick

cases.name: beam_connections
cases.description: Three wood connections along a cantilever under one tip load. Only the root connection exceeds its bending strength; it fails after a bounded number of ticks while the other two keep their full integrity and the assembly is not deleted.

rows.label: connection 1 at 6 wu from the tip, moment 600: fails after 2 ticks
connection 2 at 4 wu from the tip, moment 400: intact after 400 ticks
connection 3 at 2 wu from the tip, moment 200: intact after 400 ticks

cases.name: partition
cases.description: Splitting one contact into equivalent colliders must not multiply energy. Merged sub-contacts reproduce the single contact exactly; charging each part with the whole event would overstate the damage several times over.

rows.label: one contact: width 0.049 wu
four equivalent sub-contacts merged: width 0.049 wu
four sub-contacts each charged with the whole event, which an adapter must not do

cases.name: fixed_step
cases.description: The plank press and a connection moment just past their safe limits, stepped at 30, 60, 120 and 240 Hz, where 240 Hz is the 60 Hz tick with four substeps. The fallback is integrated exactly over each call, so the work consumed and the integrity after 1/30 s, in column a, match at every rate, and each failure lands within one tick of the continuous failure time. The other columns describe the tick that ends at 1/30 s, which shrinks as the rate rises.

rows.label: 1.05x press on the plank at 30 Hz: fails after 2 ticks (0.067 s)
1.05x press on the plank at 60 Hz: fails after 3 ticks (0.050 s)
1.05x press on the plank at 120 Hz: fails after 5 ticks (0.042 s)
1.05x press on the plank at 240 Hz: fails after 9 ticks (0.038 s)

1.08x moment on a connection at 120 Hz: fails after 6 ticks (0.050 s)
1.08x moment on a connection at 240 Hz: fails after 11 ticks (0.046 s)
